newsitem.title: UK: European strocks jump as Greenspan nerves subside.
newsitem.headline: European strocks jump as Greenspan nerves subside.

text.p: European stocks climbed strongly on Tuesday, with investors encouraged by a strong Wall Street and apparently unworried by the prospect of testimony this week from U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan.

On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar softened from earlier highs against the mark. But analysts said it would remain strong, reflecting the fact that the U.S. economy is stronger than Germany's.

French and German stocks led the way in percentage terms, with the CAC-40 index in Paris jumping 38.49 points or 1.5 percent to 2,606.34 by late morning, albeit below the record high of 2,634.48 set on February 17.
Dealers cited Wall Street, where the Dow Jones average jumped 76.58 points, or 1.1 percent, overnight to 7,008.20 due to an upbeat U.S. economy, a strong dollar and low inflation.
Germany performed well for the same reasons as Paris, with the DAX gaining 48.47 points or 1.52 percent to 3,232.68.
London gained a more modest 0.49 percent, with the FTSE 100 index up 21.2 points at 4,352.3. But that was only 10 points below its record high.

London dealers said the markets should manage further gains as long as Wall Street held firm. "The Dow has gone through 7,000 and we are just playing catch-up," said the head of equity trading at one brokerage.
"Institutions are long of cash and it just feels like we are going to have a further rally," he said. "If Wall Street holds at these levels we will move up again."

Investors seemed to have set aside, for the time being at least, their traditional wariness before the U.S. central bank chief speaks. Greenspan delivers his semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins report on the state of the U.S. economy to Congress this week and next.

Earlier in this year's bull run, Greenspan provoked nervousness among investors whenever he was due to speak. Last autumn they were badly caught out when he wiped billions of dollars off share prices worldwide by warning them of "irrational exuberance" on the markets.
Since then, Greenspan has delivered a gentler assessment of the markets, and interest rates have remained stable as the U.S. economy has achieved steady growth with low inflation.
But investors will be keeping a careful watch on Greenspan when he testifies to the Senate Banking Committee at 1500 GMT on Wednesday and to a House Banking subcommittee on March 5.
Analysts expect him to deliver a positive report but he may include some words of caution about the course of inflation and possibly the stock market.

The dollar was relatively quiet, standing at late morning at 1.6758 marks, off its high but above its late European level of 1.6700 on Monday. Against the yen, it slipped to 121.88 from its late Monday level of 122.05.

"We tried the highs against both (the mark and yen) but it was then sold off quite aggressively. It looks like we might be seeing that sort of thing on rallies now, so the dollar's looking pretty heavy," said a trader at a Japanese bank in London.
But analysts said these slight variations made little difference to the economic fundamentals.
Recent German data which were slightly better than expectations were not enough to shake the general perception of a strong U.S. economy and weakness in Germany's.

"Data in the weeks and months ahead will probably show a bit of a weakening in the U.S. economy and probably show an improvement in Germany," said Nigel Richardson, international economist at Yamaichi International in London.
"But in terms of absolute rates of growth, we'll still see relative strength in the U.S. rather than in Germany."
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6758 marks and 121.88 yen, compared with 1.6700 and 122.05 in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1130 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 21.2 points at 4,352.3.
PARIS - The CAC-40 rose 38.49 points to 2,606.34.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was 48.47 points higher at 3,232.68.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the morning at $353.45 an ounce compared with a $353.15 London close on Monday. Silver was down two cents at $5.20.
